newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom slashes call rates.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom slashes call rates.

text.p: France Telecom said on Thursday it was slashing its call rates and offering new kinds of subscriptions ahead of the total liberalisation of the telecommunications market in 1998.
The state-owned operator, due to be partially privatised this spring, said it would cut national call rates by 17.5 percent on March 4 and a further 21 percent in October 1997.
This will bring standard call rates to 1.20 francs (22 cents) per minute by end-1997 from 2.30 francs in 1994 (eds correct).
International rates will be slashed by 20 percent in March, putting all European countries at less than 2.50 francs per minute and North America at less than three francs.
France Telecom said it would raise its monthly subscription to 68 francs per month, a rise of 15.20 francs but added this was still one of the lowest rates in Europe.
From July, business clients will pay 12 francs more per month.
From March, households which hardly use the telephone can have a 34 franc monthly subscription but will then pay double rates.
In 1998 there will also be a special low monthly subscription for the socially deprived, but the government still has to decide who will qualify for it.

From October 1997, France Telecom will switch to rates based on seconds, instead of units, and will replace its current four time zones to only two -- full rates during the week from 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) to 7 p.m. (1900 GMT) and on Saturday from 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) to 12 p.m. (1100 GMT). Other times there will be at half rate. ($ = 5.226 French Francs)
